bull.b: Strong ARR growth and 126% net revenue retention indicate expanding use within Axon's installed base. This supports durable recurring revenue, higher customer lifetime value and ecosystem stickiness across devices, evidence management and software.

bull.t: Broad growth and contracted demand visibility
bull.b: Growth is broad across software, devices and platform solutions, while raised guidance and contracted bookings improve forward visibility. Multi-year public-sector deployments can support sustained expansion beyond individual hardware purchase cycles.

bull.t: Software expansion and strong gross-profit profile
bull.b: Faster software growth and increasing revenue from offerings beyond core Evidence diversify the platform and deepen customer workflows. Combined with a roughly 59%-63% gross-margin profile, this provides a foundation for scalable economics.

bear.t: Volatile profitability and modest net margins
bear.b: Although gross margins are strong, operating results have been uneven and recent net profitability remains modest. This suggests costs, mix or one-time items can materially affect earnings, limiting confidence in consistent operating leverage.

bear.t: Cash conversion and coverage remain weak
bear.b: Axon generates positive cash, but free cash flow trails accounting earnings and operating cash flow provides limited coverage of obligations. Sustained investment in inventory and growth could therefore constrain internally funded expansion.

bear.t: Meaningful debt load and reduced returns
bear.b: Leverage is manageable and improving, but the absolute debt burden has increased over earlier years while returns on equity have cooled. This reduces financial flexibility if growth slows or product investment requires additional capital.
